about.title: Coachella Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Coachella's mix of agricultural operations, family markets, and busy retail stretches near Cesar Chavez Street and Grapefruit Boulevard means residents and visitors are constantly moving through parking lots, warehouses, and store aisles owned by someone else. When a property owner lets a spill sit, ignores a broken step, or ignores a cracked sidewalk, the people walking through that space pay the price. California law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to correct or warn about it. That's why what happens right after a fall matters: photos of the surface, a written incident report, and a request to preserve any surveillance footage can make the difference in a later claim. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself. We simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can review your fall, explain your options, and take on the burden of building your case while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Coachella Premises Case

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records to establish that timeline.

items.title: Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Coachella businesses recycle surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to send a preservation request can prevent that evidence from being erased.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery — your share of fault simply adjusts the final amount rather than barring you outright.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Coachella?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a city, county, or other government entity, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. An attorney can confirm which timeline applies to your situation.

items.question: What if I fell at a store or lot near Grapefruit Boulevard or 52nd Avenue but didn't report it right away?
items.answer: Not reporting immediately doesn't automatically end your claim, but it can make proving notice and causation harder. Try to document the location, take photos if you're still able, and identify any witnesses as soon as possible. An independent attorney can help gather what evidence still exists.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. We simply help match you with someone who handles premises liability cases.
